newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong sceptics choose "pink chips" over red.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong sceptics choose "pink chips" over red.

text.p: Veteran Hong Kong analysts say they are employing the same healthy level of scepticism towards red chip newcomers as they would with any other new issue and often prefer "pink chips" to red.

"Pink chips are stocks like China Light and Power, Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd," said Carlton Poon, research director at Worldsec International. "There are quite a few but these are the main ones."
"Pink chip" is a term Poon said he has copyrighted and refers to a blue chip company that takes on significant China investment exposure.
"That is what happens when a staid, dull Hong Kong utility goes into China," said Poon.
"With my pink chips I can actually make very good profit projections of the Hong Kong earnings stream, and the China earnings stream adds a little bit of sex appeal to it," he said.
Poon said he believed red chips would pull up the Hong Kong market to 20,000 points by early 1998. On Monday, the blue chip Hang Seng Index closed at 13,987.
"But our clients have criticised us, saying it was irresponsible to present a theorectical justification for the booming rise in prices in the market," Poon said.
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated and listed companies with a China-based parent company.

Few red chips have a long track record as a listed company. Many have uncertain earnings outlooks and have soared to price/earnings ratios well beyond the average historical trading range of the market's blue chip sector.
"Why not buy HSBC Holdings or Hongkong Chinese Bank ?" said Poon, citing the two companies as good proxies for investing in China's finance sector.
Other heads of research are equally cautious in their approach to red chips.

John Pinkel, vice president in charge of China equity research at Merrill Lynch, has selected only three red chips as quality investment targets -- China Resources Enterprise Ltd, Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd and CITIC Pacific Ltd.
His China investment strategy also calls for increased exposure to Hong Kong's blue chips with a good portfolio of China assets and operations.

"We favour a strategy of buying selected high quality red chips on weakness, adding exposure through upcoming red chip IPOs (initial public offerings), and a gradual shift to some of Hong Kong's more savvy blue chips such as New World Development and Cheung Kong," Pinkel said in a recent research report.
New World Development Co Ltd has found a profitable niche in the China property market and has additional exposure through its New World Infrastructure Ltd unit, analysts said.

Both New World and Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd have a China-savvy management team which in many ways makes them comparable to red chips when red chips lose the ability to grow through injections, Pinkel said.
